subject: Containment-to-Commitment: incident summary + QBR deliverables
messages:
From: kimberly_park
To: vivek_kulkarni, marissa_cole
Cc: hannah_schmitt, ops@edgeretail.co
Date: 2027-04-25T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Incident containment summary (APAC cache lag) + immediate asks for QBR pack

Team — quick summary of the morning incident so we have a single source for execs and the QBR slide:  

What happened (high level):
- At 03:12 UTC we observed persistent KV cache lag on our APAC Dedicated pools serving EdgeRetail traffic. Cache miss amplification caused tail latency spikes and partial request throttling on their critical payment path.  
- Impact window: 03:12–05:40 UTC. We met SLA targets after failover at 05:40 but customer reported elevated error rates and higher p99 latency for ~2.5 hours.

Root cause (current hypothesis):
- A subtle regression in the cache eviction heuristic deployed in the 2027-04-24 runtime build. Under a specific sequence-length distribution, the heuristic failed to free older KV entries fast enough, causing memory pressure and increased I/O to remote store.

Mitigation taken:
- Hotfix rolled back at 04:22 UTC (marissa).
- Emergency autoscaling policy applied to affected Dedicated pool at 04:25 UTC; additional nodes brought online, and traffic was rebalanced.
- Full failover to fallback region completed by 05:40 UTC.

Metrics (preliminary):
- SLA violations recorded: 14 distinct 5m windows; total customer-facing error count ~430 (EdgeRetail telemetry).
- p99 latency increased from ~210ms to ~1.8s during peak.
- No customer data exfiltration or config drift identified.

Immediate asks for QBR slide deck:  
1) A one-page exec summary that states impact, root-cause, customer pain, and immediate corrective commitments (owners + dates). (Vivek: please review tone.)
2) A concise action table for the QBR appendix with owners, ETA, and acceptance criteria.
3) Include three artifacts as supplemental evidence: incident_timeline.csv, kv-cache-lag-snapshot.png, the draft one-pager qbr_one_pager.docx.

Attachments linked here and in the postmortem doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/pm/EDGE-INC-0424-postmortem

I'll circulate a cleaned one-pager by noon PT; Marissa please confirm the RCA items below and owners so I can lock the slide.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: vivek_kulkarni
To: kimberly_park
Cc: marissa_cole, hannah_schmitt
Date: 2027-04-25T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Incident containment summary (APAC cache lag) + immediate asks for QBR pack

Kimberly — thanks for the clear summary. Two requests before we publish to the exec QBR packet:  

1) Make the first slide zero-technical: "What happened, customer impact (quantified), and our commitment" in five bullets. Keep the technical appendix separate.
2) For each action item, add the measurable acceptance criteria (e.g., "reduce p99 to <300ms under X workload", "deploy new eviction heuristic behind canary with 48h soak").

Marissa — I need a short note from you confirming the hotfix rollback timestamp, the autoscale knobs we flipped, and whether a code revert is required vs. config tuning. Please keep it bulletized (max 6 lines).

I'll review Kimberly's one-pager once it's in Drive. Aim to have the final slide set to me by EOD so we can tie in the OKR implications.

Vivek
CEO, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole
To: kimberly_park, vivek_kulkarni
Cc: hannah_schmitt
Date: 2027-04-25T13:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Incident containment summary (APAC cache lag) + immediate asks for QBR pack

On Sun, Apr 25, 2027 at 11:12 AM Vivek Kulkarni wrote:
> Kimberly — thanks for the clear summary. Two requests before we publish to the exec QBR packet:  
> 
> 1) Make the first slide zero-technical...

Notes & action items (tech bullets for the appendix):
- Hotfix rollback confirmed: 2027-04-25T04:22:13 UTC (rolled back to runtime v2027-04-23-19). (evidence: incident_timeline.csv line 42)
- Autoscale policy change: temporarily raised dedicated-pool cap by +30% and lowered request queue threshold from 0.8 to 0.6 at 04:25 UTC. This prevented node OOMs but did not stop higher remote-store I/O immediately.
- Repro & RCA plan: we have a deterministic repro on synthetic trace #R-APR24-7 (attached to the postmortem). Root cause tied to eviction-order change in commit c3b9f8; fix options:
  • revert commit c3b9f8 (fastest) — owner: marissa_cole — ETA: 48h for canary and 72h for full rollout. Acceptance: canary p99 <350ms for 48h under replay test.
  • implement a hybrid eviction fallback (safer) — owner: infra-engineering — ETA: 3 weeks. Acceptance: validated under chaos testing and e2e regression.
- Customer remediation: proactively opened a credits request with EdgeRetail (ops@edgeretail.co) and offered a technical postmortem session.

Open asks for QBR slide/table (owners assigned):
- One-pager with non-technical impact summary: Owner: kimberly_park — Draft due: 2027-04-25T12:30 PT. (Kim — please confirm you uploaded qbr_one_pager.docx.)
- Revert + canary plan signoff: Owner: marissa_cole — Draft ETA: 2027-04-27T10:00 PT.
- OKR observable update (reliability): Owner: hannah_schmitt — Confirm how this incident factors into Q2 reliability OKR (slack/metric deltas) — ETA: 2027-04-27T17:00 PT.

I uploaded the artifacts to the postmortem link and attached a small CSV and a snapshot png for the QBR. Let me know if you need raw KV traces.

—Marissa
Sr. SRE Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: incident_timeline.csv, kv-cache-lag-snapshot.png

Thanks all — short notes:  

- Kimberly: the one-pager looks good; please publish the finalized qbr_one_pager.docx to the shared QBR folder and mark it as "Exec-ready." I pulled it into the QBR deck draft and flagged an appendix slide for the technical RCA.
- Marissa: confirm the revert plan (I support the revert + canary path) and stamp the acceptance criteria as Vivek requested. Ensure the canary runs for 48h with telemetry visible in the QBR dashboard.
- I've updated the OKR tracker to reflect a temporary dip in Availability and added the incident as a reliability risk with link to the postmortem. Owners: Marissa (technical fix), Kimberly (customer remediation & exec comms), Hannah (OKR rollforward).

I'll notify Growth and Sales to expect a customer postmortem session this week; Kimberly, please coordinate times with EdgeRetail.

Hannah Schmitt
